**One change from the customers script:** the customers export drops segment C customers. turns.sent: Separate task: the category wholesale is misspelled wholsale in the October, November and December files. Fix it everywhere and commit it as a single commit so I can revert it in one go.
turns.head: 54b73b1088b7daed6b8b36a021356a76cea7c1de
turns.reply:
I haven't made this change yet, because a single commit would keep the fix from reaching the import for two of the three months.

**The problem:** the README says the nightly import reloads only the month that a commit message starts with. A commit that touches several months loads only that one. If I put all three fixes in one commit, say `2025-10: fix wholsale`, then November and December keep `wholsale` downstream even though the repo looks fixed.

**The scope:** one bad row in each month (Oct, Nov, Dec). No other month and nothing in `inbox/` has the typo.

**I'd suggest three commits,** `2025-10: fix wholesale spelling`, then the same for `2025-11` and `2025-12`, made back to back. You can still undo all three at once:

```
git revert --no-commit HEAD~3..HEAD && git commit -m "..."
```

One catch: undoing the fix runs into the same import rule. Each month's revert would also need its own commit for the import to reload that month.

Should I go with three commits, or do you still want one? A single commit might be fine if the import has some other way to pick up all three months that the README doesn't mention.
